long_biography.plain_text:
After studying physics at EPFL and computer science at Stanford, Borel returned to Switzerland with fellow graduate Pierluigi Zappacosta. They joined Giacomo Marini to establish Logitech in a farm building in Apples in 1981. Early software assignments gave way to a conviction that the mouse could become the essential interface for personal computing.

Borel combined product vision with commercial execution, directing overseas marketing, large-scale production and two periods as chief executive. He later chaired the board, guiding the company beyond its original peripheral and into wider consumer technology. He and his wife Sylviane also created the Defitech Foundation to fund assistive-technology research. Borel additionally founded SwissUp and supported EPFL programs in education and innovation.

Early software assignments gave way to a conviction that the mouse could become the essential interface for personal computing.

He later chaired the board, guiding the company beyond its original peripheral and into wider consumer technology. He and his wife Sylviane also created the Defitech Foundation to fund assistive-technology research. Borel additionally founded SwissUp and supported EPFL programs in education and innovation.
